title: Darwin's Theory of Evolution
subject: sciences
description: In 1859, Darwin published On the Origin of Species. The core idea: living things change over time through natural selection.

hero.hook: Species are not fixed. They change. Slowly. But surely.

blocks.text: In **1859**, **Charles Darwin** published *On the Origin of Species*. The book shocked, thrilled, and divided its readers. Its central idea, though, is simple to state.
Living things vary. Some variations help them survive and reproduce. Those variations are passed on. Generation after generation, populations change.

sections.title: The voyage that opened his eyes

blocks.caption: Darwin, the British naturalist of the 19th century

blocks.text: As a young man, Darwin sailed on the ship **Beagle**. For years he studied plants, fossils, and birds. In the Galapagos Islands, he noticed that closely related birds had different beaks depending on what they ate.

blocks.caption: Beaks matched to different diets: a powerful clue

blocks.text: Imagine a population of animals. Some run a little faster, digest a little better, stand the cold a little longer. If that helps them survive and have young, those traits become more common.
It is not that individuals “want” to evolve. It is a filter: the environment tends to keep what works. Darwin called this **natural selection**.
Darwin waited a long time before publishing. He feared the scandal. Another naturalist, **Alfred Russel Wallace**, reached very similar ideas, and that pushed Darwin to bring out his book.

In the 19th century, many people believed that species had been created exactly as they are. Saying that they change, and that humans share a history with other animals, unsettled both religion and society.
Science, for its part, moved forward: fossils, the geography of species, and later genetics all confirmed the general idea.

We now know that DNA carries the variations. Evolution can be watched in the lab (bacteria, viruses) and in the wild. We also fight bacteria that resist antibiotics, and that is evolution happening live.
Darwin showed that life evolves by natural selection: the traits that help survival and reproduction spread. Modern genetics has confirmed and sharpened that framework.
